newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, AGAs have little impact.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, AGAs have little impact.

text.p: NYMEX Hub natgas futures ended mixed Wednesday in another sluggish session, with front months buoyed early by short covering, then reacting very little in overnight ACCESS trade after the weekly gas inventory report.

April edged up 0.9 cent to close at $1.865 per million British thermal units, then traded on ACCESS on either side of unchanged after AGA stock data. May settled one cent higher at $1.908, while most others ended down slightly.
"It (the AGA number) was way under expectations, but it's a non-event. The market is already priced for too much inventory," said one Houston-based trader.

AGA said U.S. gas stocks fell last week by 63 bcf, well-below expectations in the 80-95 bcf range. Overall stocks are still 144 bcf, or 16 percent, above year-ago. Eastern inventories, which fell by 58 bcf, remained a hefty 225 bcf, or 56 percent, over last year's levels.

With fairly mild weather ahead and storage, particularly in the East, more than adequate to meet any incremental March demand, few expected a significant cash or paper rally any time soon. But some said prices may be nearing bottom.

While chart traders did not rule out a technical bounce, most expected futures to drift within recent ranges until clearer signs emerge from the March cash next week. April support was still seen at $1.80, then in the mid-$1.70s and the contract low of $1.701. Resistance was pegged along the down trendline in the $1.90 area, then at $1.935 and $2.04.

In the physical market, March Gulf Coast gas edged up slightly Wednesday to the mid-to-high $1.70s. March Midcon gas also was talked modestly higher in the mid-$1.60s. New York city gate for March was little changed in the $2.10-15 area.
The 12-month strip fell 0.6 cent to $2.04. NYMEX said an estimated 21,033 Hub contracts traded, down from Tuesday's revised tally of 30,371.
NYMEX Permian natgas did not trade Wednesday. Alberta natgas traded two lots.
On the KCBT, April finished four cents higher at $1.63, while deferreds ended up by three to five cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.1 cent to 24.4 cents (NYMEX premium).
